sentences.text: Redondasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur, a group of armored reptiles.
Unlike other aetosaurs with radially patterned scutes, Redondasuchus scutes are densely pitted but lack any specific patterning, and its dorsal paramedian scutes are angled approximately 45 degrees.
In both Redondasuchus species, each paramedian scute has an underside keel extending from the medial edge to the flexed area.
The dorsal paramedian scutes of Redondasuchus are unique because they are angled approximately 45 degrees.
Its scutes are densely pitted but lack any specific patterning, unlike other aetosaurs.

The type species R. reseri was named in 1991 based on isolated scutes found at Apache Canyon and Shark Tooth Hill in Quay County, New Mexico, though it had previously been classified as a species of Typothorax since 1985.
A second species, R. rineharti, was described in 2006.
Redondasuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Heckert et al. (1996) classified Redondasuchus as part of an advanced grade of aetosaurs alongside Neoaetosauroides, Longosuchus, Desmatosuchus, Paratypothorax, and Typothorax.
Fossils of Redondasuchus have been found in the Redonda Formation in east-central New Mexico.
Redondasuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
Jeffrey Martz suggested that R. reseri is synonymous with Typothorax coccinarum, a hypothesis that remains debated.
An independent investigation by the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology found no evidence of explicit, intentional plagiarism in the 2006 paper describing Redondasuchus.
